The best free tools to watermark photos in bulk

Photographers, shops and agents need the same logo or © line on a whole set of pictures. These four tools all do batches; they differ in what the free version leaves on your photos and where the files go.

We make Slop Watermark, one of the tools on this page. Every fact about the other tools comes from their own pages, linked under each one, as they read on 2026-10-24. Prices and features change: check each site before you choose.

How we compared them

  • The free version leaves only your watermark, not one of its own
  • Batch size and other free limits
  • Where the photos are processed
  • Watermark options: logo, text, tiling, rotation, opacity

1. Slop Watermark (ours)

Best for: A free batch of up to 500 photos with your logo or text and no mark of its own, without uploading anything.

Good

  • Logo or text, nine positions, tiling and rotation from -90° to 90°
  • Logo sized to each picture, with separate settings for portrait, landscape, square and panorama
  • Live preview, then apply to all; download each file or a ZIP
  • Pictures keep their pixel size; the setup is remembered in your browser

Not so good

  • Still in beta
  • Pictures only: no PDFs or videos here (SlopCut can watermark video)
  • No mobile app
  • GIFs are saved as still PNGs; very large pictures are capped at 8000 pixels on the long side

Open Slop Watermark

2. Watermarkly

Best for: People who want apps on every device and also watermark PDFs and videos, and will pay to remove its logo.

Good

  • Text and logo watermarks with over 900 fonts, opacity and rotation
  • Web app, desktop apps and mobile apps; PDFs and video on some of them
  • Saved templates synced across devices
  • Says files stay in your browser and are not stored on its servers

Not so good

  • The free version adds a Watermarkly logo next to yours
  • Video only in the Windows, Mac and iOS apps

Watermarkly website · Sources: Watermarkly home, Watermarkly pricing, Watermarkly: tile mode

3. Visual Watermark

Best for: Offline desktop batches with tiling and 100 opacity levels, after a free trial.

Good

  • Desktop app for Windows and macOS that works offline: images never reach its server
  • Tiling, rotation and 100 levels of transparency
  • Batch processing on all CPU cores; keeps EXIF and IPTC in JPEGs
  • Outputs JPEG, PNG, TIFF, GIF and BMP

Not so good

  • A trial, not a free plan: trial output carries its own text
  • An install for the desktop version

Visual Watermark website · Sources: Visual Watermark home, Visual Watermark buy page

4. iLoveIMG

Best for: A quick online batch of up to 30 pictures, alongside its other image tools.

Good

  • Image or text watermark with font, colour, opacity and shadow
  • Imports from Google Drive and Dropbox
  • Part of a set of web image tools, with an API

Not so good

  • Free tasks are limited to 30 files and 200 MB, with ads
  • Files are uploaded to its servers for processing
  • Mobile access only with Premium

iLoveIMG website · Sources: iLoveIMG watermark tool, iLoveIMG pricing, iLoveIMG FAQ, iLoveIMG watermark tutorial, iLoveIMG terms

Which one to choose

On the criteria of this page, a free result with only your own mark and photos kept on your device, Slop Watermark fits best, which is why it is first. It does pictures only, in the browser.

Watermarkly and Visual Watermark have more: PDFs, video, desktop and mobile apps, but the free versions put their own mark on your photos until you pay. iLoveIMG is handy for a quick online batch of up to 30 files.

Questions

Which free watermark tool does not add its own logo?

Slop Watermark adds only your watermark. Watermarkly's free version adds a Watermarkly logo and Visual Watermark's trial adds trial text, by their own pages. iLoveIMG's pages do not say.

How many photos can I watermark at once for free?

Slop Watermark takes up to 500 pictures at a time and iLoveIMG up to 30 files per task. Watermarkly and Visual Watermark do batches but do not state a free number.

Are my photos uploaded?

Slop Watermark stamps them in your browser. Watermarkly says files stay in your browser, Visual Watermark's desktop app works offline, and iLoveIMG processes files on its servers and deletes them after download.

Can I watermark a video or PDF?

Not in Slop Watermark; SlopCut can put a watermark on a video. Watermarkly and Visual Watermark do PDFs and video in some of their apps.
